section_1.title: Conceptual Foundations (Prerequisites)
section_1.content: Define vectors as directed line segments. Introduce the 'Right-Hand Rule' as the fundamental constraint for 3D orientation. Briefly explain that while the dot product yields a scalar (projection), the cross product generates a new vector perpendicular to the original plane.
section_1.example: Visualizing a clock hand: The vector points towards the center of the clock, representing the axis of rotation.

section_2.title: 2D 'Cross Product' as Oriented Area
section_2.content: Explain the 2D cross product (determinant of a 2x2 matrix). Crucially, frame this as the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by two vectors. If the sequence is counter-clockwise, the result is positive; clockwise results in negative.
section_2.example: A robot arm in 2D space moving between vectors (1,0) and (0,1); the area is 1, representing the space swept by the arm.

section_3.title: The 3D Cross Product Mechanics
section_3.content: Extend to 3D using the determinant expansion (i, j, k unit vectors). Emphasize that the magnitude |a × b| = |a||b|sin(θ). Use a 3D animation showing the resulting vector 'growing' out of the plane as the angle between the two base vectors changes.
section_3.example: A spinning propeller blade: The two vectors are the blade length and the spin force; the cross product represents the resulting thrust vector pushing the aircraft forward.

section_4.title: Geometric Interpretations & Applications
section_4.content: Summarize the utility: 1. Finding a normal vector to a surface (essential for computer graphics lighting). 2. Calculating torque in physics. Reinforce that if the cross product is zero, vectors are collinear.
section_4.example: A monkey turning a wrench: The force applied to the handle (vector 1) at a distance from the bolt (vector 2) creates a torque vector (cross product) that drives the bolt into the wall.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
